breathing_trouble.question: Is your cat struggling to breathe, or breathing very fast while resting?
breathing_trouble.help: Count the breaths for a minute while your cat rests (each rise and fall of the chest is one). More than 35 a minute is too fast.
breathing_trouble.why: Trouble breathing needs a vet straight away, whatever the cause.

collapsed.question: Has your cat collapsed, or is it unable to stand up?
collapsed.help: Lying flat and not getting up, falling over when it tries to walk, or not responding to you.
collapsed.why: A cat that has collapsed needs a vet straight away, whatever the cause.

blood_in_stool.question: Is there blood in your cat's stool or vomit?
blood_in_stool.help: Red streaks or spots, or very dark, tarry stool.
blood_in_stool.why: Blood in the stool or vomit is a danger sign. Cat Parvo can cause bloody diarrhoea.

straining.question: Is your cat straining in the litter box?
straining.help: Squatting for a long time and pushing, getting up and trying again. Owners often mistake this for constipation.
straining.why: Straining to urinate is the main sign of a bladder problem, and can mean the bladder is blocked.

litter_often.question: Is your cat going to the litter box much more often than usual?
litter_often.help: Many short visits, or trying to go outside the litter box.
litter_often.why: Going much more often is a common sign of a bladder problem.

little_urine.question: When it tries, does your cat pass only a little urine, or none at all?
little_urine.help: Check the litter: only small wet spots, a few drops, or nothing at all count as yes.
little_urine.why: Straining with little or no urine means the urine cannot get out. Cornell calls this an absolute emergency.

cries_urinating.question: Does your cat cry or yowl when it tries to urinate?
cries_urinating.help: Crying, growling or yowling while in the litter box.
cries_urinating.why: Crying while urinating shows pain, a sign of a bladder problem.

blood_in_urine.question: Is there blood in your cat's urine?
blood_in_urine.help: Pink, red or brown urine, or red spots in the litter.
blood_in_urine.why: Blood in the urine is a sign of a bladder problem.

licking_genitals.question: Is your cat licking its genital area much more than usual?
licking_genitals.help: Licking under the tail again and again, often after visiting the litter box.
licking_genitals.why: Frequent licking of the genital area is a sign of a bladder problem.

sex.question: Is your cat male or female?
sex.help: Answer male even if he has been neutered.
sex.why: Male cats are at greater risk of a blocked bladder because their urethra is longer and narrower.

sneezing.question: Is your cat sneezing?
sneezing.help: Sneezing more than a few times a day counts.
sneezing.why: Sneezing is one of the main signs of Cat Flu.

eye_discharge.question: Is there discharge from your cat's eyes?
eye_discharge.help: Watery, sticky, yellow or green discharge, or crust in the corners of the eyes.
eye_discharge.why: Eye discharge is one of the main signs of Cat Flu.

nose_discharge.question: Is there discharge from your cat's nose?
nose_discharge.help: A runny or crusty nose, clear or coloured.
nose_discharge.why: Nose discharge is one of the main signs of Cat Flu.

red_eyes.question: Are your cat's eyes red or swollen around the edges?
red_eyes.help: Look at the pink skin around the eyes: red, puffy or half-closed eyes count.
red_eyes.why: Red, swollen eyes (conjunctivitis) often come with Cat Flu.

mouth_sores.question: Are there sores in your cat's mouth, or is it drooling?
mouth_sores.help: Red spots or ulcers on the tongue or gums, or wet fur on the chin.
mouth_sores.why: Calicivirus, one of the Cat Flu viruses, can sometimes cause mouth ulcers.

near_other_cats.question: Has your cat been near other cats recently?
near_other_cats.help: For example a new cat at home, going outdoors, a cattery, a shelter or a pet shop.
near_other_cats.why: Cat Flu and Cat Parvo spread between cats, especially where many cats are kept together.

vomiting.question: Is your cat vomiting?
vomiting.help: Bringing up food, liquid or foam. A single hairball does not count.
vomiting.why: Vomiting is one of the main signs of Cat Parvo.

diarrhoea.question: Does your cat have diarrhoea?
diarrhoea.help: Loose or watery stool, in or outside the litter box.
diarrhoea.why: Diarrhoea is one of the main signs of Cat Parvo.

age.question: How old is your cat?
age.help: Type the age, for example "6 months", "2 years" or "kitten". Cats under 1 year old count as kittens.
age.why: Kittens are the group most at risk of Cat Parvo, and get very sick very quickly.

vaccinated.question: Has your cat had its vaccinations?
vaccinated.help: The core cat vaccine is called FVRCP (sometimes "tricat"). Check the vaccination card, or ask whoever gave you the cat.
vaccinated.why: Vaccination protects against Cat Parvo. Unvaccinated cats and kittens are the main group that catches it.

tired.question: Is your cat unusually tired, weak or hiding?
tired.help: Sleeping much more than usual, not wanting to play, hiding under furniture, or weak on its legs.
tired.why: Tiredness and weakness show the cat is generally unwell.

appetite.question: Is your cat eating?
appetite.help: Compare with how much it usually eats.
appetite.why: Not eating is a sign of illness, and a cat that eats nothing for about a day needs a vet.

hours_since_ate.question: How long is it since your cat last ate anything?
hours_since_ate.help: Type it in hours or days, for example "10 hours", "2 days" or "since yesterday".
hours_since_ate.why: A cat that eats nothing for about 24 hours should see a vet the same day, because not eating can quickly cause liver problems.

temperature.question: What is your cat's temperature?
temperature.help: Only if you have a pet thermometer: type it like "102.5 F" or "39 C". Normal is about 100.5–102.5 °F (38.1–39.2 °C). If you can't measure it, answer "not sure".
temperature.why: A high temperature (fever) shows the body is fighting an infection.

danger_sign.label: your cat has a danger sign that needs a vet straight away

urinary_signs.label: your cat is having trouble urinating

urine_blocked.label: urine cannot get out of the bladder

respiratory_signs.label: your cat has signs of a nose and eye infection (sneezing or discharge)

gi_signs.label: your cat has stomach or gut signs (vomiting or diarrhoea)

parvo_risk.label: your cat is in the group most at risk of Cat Parvo (a kitten or unvaccinated)

systemic_illness.label: your cat is generally unwell (tired, not eating or feverish)
